shadow:
There is a hunger in the body that has no name and no end. You feed it and it goes quiet for an hour, then it lifts its head again and points at something new. The thing it wants keeps changing. The wanting does not.

Most people read this as a moral failing, something to be starved out or apologised for. That reading is the whole trap. The hunger is not a fault in the wiring, it is the wiring. It was put there to push people out into experience, to make them touch things they would never have chosen, and a life that refuses it stays small.

The heaviness comes from the fight, not the hunger. Treat the wanting as shameful and it grows teeth. Tell yourself a real person would have outgrown this by now, and every ordinary craving becomes evidence against you. The mind catches one small desire and inflates it until it blocks the light.

The fire clings. You cannot put it out and you were never meant to. What can change is how heavily you carry it. The way through is not less hunger. It is less story wrapped around the hunger, which is slower work than it sounds.
repressive: Some people answer the hunger by going stern. They lay rules over every craving, decide that wanting is beneath them, and let the inner fire bank down to ash. It looks like discipline. Underneath, the life force has gone stiff and grey.
reactive: Others answer it by chasing every spark. They follow each desire to its end, scorn anyone who counsels restraint, and call it freedom. The fire is real, but it is uncontrolled. They tend to burn through themselves fast and early.
gift:
Something loosens when a person stops treating their own wanting as a court case. The hunger is still there. What leaves is the verdict.

This is lightness, and it is not the lightness of making a joke to skip past something hard. It is closer to the opposite. You go further into the feeling than before, you let the craving be fully felt, and you do that without being dragged off your feet by it. A desire arrives. You notice it the way you notice a guest at the door. Some guests sit a while and leave on their own. Some insist on being walked out into the world before they will go. Either way you are no longer their hostage.

There is humour in this, the kind that turns on yourself first. You watch yourself reach for the thing, get the thing, feel the old emptiness reopen a day later, and instead of despair there is something almost tender about it. The reaching was never going to land. Knowing that does not kill the hunger. It loosens the grip, so the same fuel that used to weigh the body down starts to lift it. Underneath the thousand small wants, one longing pulls upward.
siddhi:
Now every desire has poured back into one. Not the wanting of this or that, but the pure ache underneath all of it, the longing that has no object and was never really about objects at all.

A person here is flammable. The smallest thing sets them alight, a name, a phrase, a glance, and the fire does not hurt anymore. It is bliss, returning and returning. Whoever stands near tends to catch it. This is rapture, and it looks like madness to a mind that needs to stay in charge, because the one who could lose control is no longer there to lose anything.

The fire clung the whole way through. It clung in the restless hunger at the start, the wanting that pointed everywhere and rested nowhere. That was not a flaw in the design. It was the same fire, unpurified, doing the only thing it knew. It was always carrying the person home. There is a word in the language that holds this quietly. To belong is to be your longing, completely, with nothing held back.
